title: Optimal Sorting Networks (Knuth Open Frontier)
tagline: World-record comparator & depth hunt · Lean 4.36.0 kernel
question: What is the minimum number of compare-and-swap steps to sort 13 numbers?
description: Prove Knuth's Zero-One Principle, reconstruct optimal sorting networks for 4 to 12 wires in pure Lean 4, and hunt for a 44-comparator 13-wire network — beating a 50-year-old human world record (current record = 45, proven lower bound = 39).
verdict: open world record hunt — accepting token donations.

tug_of_war.disclaimer: Counts Lean-verified sorting networks vs. Lean-verified impossibility/optimality bounds.

impact.ships_to: LLVM libc++ std::sort, Google Highway (vqsort), DuckDB, NVIDIA CUB / Thrust GPU warp sort, FPGA pipelines
impact.bottleneck: Modern CPU/GPU sorting libraries finish small partitions (n = 8..16 elements) using branchless SIMD min/max sorting networks inside registers. Every comparator is two vector min/max instructions; every parallel layer adds a full register-dependency latency cycle.
impact.what_one_step_buys: Removing 1 comparator or 1 parallel layer from a 16-wire network speeds up every AVX-512 (16×32-bit) and CUDA half-warp base sort in databases, search engines, and standard libraries — permanently, with zero branch mispredictions.

consumers.name: LLVM libc++ / AlphaDev std::sort
consumers.detail: Uses provably optimal fixed-size branchless sorting networks as base cases for C++ std::sort.

consumers.name: Google Highway (vqsort) & x86-simd-sort
consumers.detail: 16-lane AVX-512 sorting networks power vectorized sorting in DuckDB, ClickHouse, and NumPy.

consumers.name: NVIDIA CUB / Thrust WarpSort
consumers.detail: Depth-optimal 16- and 32-lane comparator networks execute inside GPU warp shuffle registers with zero shared memory.

examples.use_case: AVX-512 16-lane SIMD & GPU half-warp register sort
examples.mechanism: Every verified Net 16 exports directly as a branchless C/SIMD `CMP_SWAP(a, b)` macro sequence (or AVX-512 `_mm512_min/max_epi32` schedule).
examples.metric: Beating Green's 1969 record of 60 comparators on 16 wires directly shrinks instruction count for every 16-lane SIMD base sort.

examples.use_case: Low-latency FPGA & GPU pipeline sorting (16-wire depth)
examples.mechanism: Parallel depth equals exact hardware pipeline stages / critical-path latency in SIMD & Verilog.
examples.metric: Depth-9 optimal 16-wire network beats Batcher bitonic sort (depth 10) by 10% end-to-end latency.

examples.mechanism: Proving depth 9 on 17 wires (or ¬Record 9) resolves a decades-old open boundary in parallel comparison networks.
examples.metric: Direct publishable CS result checked in seconds by Lean 4's kernel.

objectives.title: Zero-One Principle & Optimal 4–5 Wire Networks
objectives.finish_line: Prove Knuth's Zero-One Principle, verify optimal 4-wire (5 steps, depth 3) & 5-wire (9 steps, depth 5) networks, and prove 4 wires cannot be sorted in ≤ 4 steps.

objectives.title: Classic Knuth Optimal Benchmarks (8, 9 & 10 Wires)
objectives.finish_line: Synthesize and Lean-verify optimal sorting networks for n=8 (19 steps, depth 6), n=9 (25 steps), and n=10 (29 steps).

objectives.title: Open World Record Frontier: 12-Wire Optimal & 13–14 Wire King of the Hill Hunts
objectives.finish_line: Verify the optimal 12-wire network (39 steps) and ratchet down the live 13-, 14-, 15-wire size & 17-wire depth King-of-the-Hill hunts.

objectives.title: AVX-512 & GPU Warp-Width 16-Wire SIMD Sorters (Size ≤ 60 & Depth ≤ 9)
objectives.finish_line: Certify Green's 60-comparator 16-wire sorter (beat 60 for a 1969 world record!) and the exact depth-9 optimal 16-wire parallel network.
